extracted.intended_audience: sellers of subscription/negative-option services, industry stakeholders, trade associations, and regulatory/legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rulemaking preamble explaining required attributes of cancellation mechanisms for negative-option/subscription services (e.g., simple cancellation, same-medium cancellation, disclosure requirements, authentication limits). Aimed at interpreting and applying the FTC's proposed Rule provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple cancellation mechanism requirement (§425.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: All cancellation mechanisms must be simple and easy to use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The simple cancellation mechanism should remove barriers such as unreasonable hold times or verification requirements. Sellers must comply with all requirements of a simple cancellation mechanism, and cannot rely on convoluted procedures to frustrate cancellation. Cited cases and commenters demonstrate harms where cancellation was made harder than enrollment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and accessible effectuation of cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumers must be able to promptly effectuate cancellation through an accessible means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sellers must ensure consumers can promptly effectuate cancellations via accessible channels; the Commission emphasized accessibility concerns (e.g., harms to disabled persons, people unable to leave home). Examples include being able to cancel without in-person travel, and avoiding practices that require excessive time or effort to locate cancellation methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow reasonable authentication/verification prior to cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonable authentication and verification procedures may be allowed prior to cancellation to ensure only authorized persons make changes to an account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters supported reasonable verification (to prevent unauthorized cancellations), but the rule should not let verification requirements become barriers that prevent timely cancellation. Industry requests to 'expressly allow' privacy and data-security measures for verification are acknowledged, but such procedures must not frustrate simple cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Same-medium cancellation (at least) — online cancellation on same website (§425.6(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: For online cancellation, sellers must provide a simple cancellation mechanism through the same website or web-based application used for sign-up (the 'Click to Cancel' provision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM explained the Click to Cancel provision requires an accessible cancellation mechanism on the same website/web-based application used for sign-up. The Commission will make conforming changes to add 'consent' language in §425.6(c)(1). Commenters urged one-click cancel if one-click enroll, and emphasized cancellation should require no more steps than enrollment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation method parity with enrollment
rubrics_metrics.description: The method provided for signing up should also be provided for cancelling the same service, be just as easy to find, and require no more steps than it took to sign up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple commenters argued 'if you signed up online, you should be able to cancel online' and that cancellation should mirror the convenience of enrollment (e.g., one click to join => one click to cancel). The Commission recognizes this expectation and cites consumer anecdotes where sign-up was trivial but cancellation required phone calls and long hold times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow at least one non-in-person cancellation mechanism for in-person sign-ups
rubrics_metrics.description: Where consent was obtained in person, the business must provide at least one cancellation mechanism in addition to in-person cancellation (e.g., telephone or online), though in-person method is required only 'where practical.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICA's comment clarified the Rule does not require both telephone and online for in-person consent; a business may elect either online or telephone (or both). N/MA noted in-person cancellation may be impossible (e.g., trade show), so the in-person method only must be available where practical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Web-based chat cancellation limited to agent-enrollment cases
rubrics_metrics.description: A web-based chat may qualify as an appropriate cancellation mechanism only if the consumer enrolled through a virtual or live agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Chamber asked to confirm web chat is appropriate; the Commission says chat is acceptable only where enrollment required engaging with an agent. The Rule precludes requiring consumers to engage with agents (live or virtual) for cancellation unless enrollment required it; this prevents asymmetrical practices used to create unfair/deceptive cancellation procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on asymmetrical agent-only cancellation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers cannot require consumers to engage with live or virtual agents to cancel when such agent interaction was not required to enroll.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record shows requiring agent interactions for cancellation but not for enrollment is a principal method to create unfair and deceptive cancellation procedures. Limitations are appropriate to prevent use of such practices (e.g., forced web chat or calls to trigger retention pitches).

rubrics_metrics.name: Seller may offer live representative but cannot make sole cancellation path
rubrics_metrics.description: Businesses may choose to have a live representative available to manage cancellations, but this cannot be the only cancellation mechanism if consumers enrolled without interacting with an agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some industry commenters wanted a live representative ability; the Commission accepts that businesses may have live agents speak with customers seeking to cancel, but the Rule should not permit sellers to require this where not required for enrollment. Exceptions for multi-product subscriptions needing assistance are recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of where to find cancellation mechanism prior to sale (§425.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers must disclose where to find the cancellation mechanism prior to the sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble cites requirements that the seller disclose where to find cancellation mechanism before sale (referencing §425.4) so consumers know how to terminate in the future; commenters requested explicit language ensuring it's 'easy to check back with the company or their subcontractors to cancel at anytime.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation mechanism should be easy to find and prominently displayed
rubrics_metrics.description: The cancellation button or instructions should be easy to locate, highlighted, and in an obvious location (as attractively marketed as extension/renewal offers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters recommended the termination button be highlighted and obvious (font size, colors, etc.). Many consumer anecdotes report difficulty finding cancellation links because they are hidden; the Rule should require straightforward, plain-language cancellation instructions that are easy to locate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on seller retention pitches during cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers should be limited in their efforts to pitch additional offers or subject consumers to protracted retention scripts when the consumer seeks to cancel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record includes many complaints about hard-sell techniques and long sales pitches during cancellation calls or chats. Commenters suggested limiting efforts to pitch additional offers or modifications; one comment suggested cancellation should not take more than about 90 seconds instead of endless questioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-pattern: sellers creating complicated signup procedures to justify complex cancellations
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers should not craft convoluted signup procedures or business practices to justify or hide complex or burdensome cancellation mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters raised concerns that sellers might create complicated signup processes to then justify complex cancellation mechanisms. The Commission warns sellers must still comply with simple cancellation requirements even if signup processes were contrived.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-law model for accessible online termination (termination email format)
rubrics_metrics.description: An acceptable online termination method may be an immediately accessible termination email formatted and provided by the business that a consumer can send without providing additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites state statutes (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §17602; Conn. Gen. Stat. §42-158ff; N.J. Stat. Ann. §56:8-42.1) that provide model language: a termination email formatted/provided by the business that consumers can send without obtaining extra information, demonstrating an acceptable design for online termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation availability across seller-used media (State AG proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: One proposal urged requiring sellers to allow all consumers to cancel through any medium that the seller uses to sell subscriptions or memberships, regardless of how the particular consumer signed up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State AGs suggested allowing cancellation via any medium the seller uses would better match consumer expectations and technology changes (e.g., online, telephone, mail), rather than strictly tying the cancellation method to the consumer's enrollment medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Click-to-Cancel must not be limited to in-game or non-expected locations
rubrics_metrics.description: Cancellation ingress must be placed in locations consumers would reasonably expect (e.g., not hidden in-game if that is not the expected place to cancel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters observed in-game interfaces are not places most players would expect to find cancellation; sellers should provide cancellation where consumers logically look to the seller to cancel the arrangement, not only in the enrollment interface if that is a third party or uncommon location.
